title: Beyond the 956: Veruschka, iconic 1960s supermodel and 'Blow-Up' star, dies at 87
excerpt: Veruschka, the German supermodel whose face defined 1960s fashion and who appeared in Michelangelo Antonioni's 'Blow-Up,' has died at 87. She died at her home in Berlin, her family confirmed.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Veruschka, the German supermodel whose striking face defined 1960s fashion and who appeared as herself in Michelangelo Antonioni's classic film "Blow-Up," has died at 87.

She died at her home in Berlin, surrounded by friends and family, according to German newspaper Bild, which reported her death on Wednesday, November 25. A relative confirmed her death to the newspaper. No cause of death was reported.

Born Vera Gottliebe Anna Gräfin von Lehndorff-Steinort in East Prussia in 1939, Veruschka's childhood was upended by World War II: her father was executed for his involvement in the failed 1944 plot to assassinate Adolf Hitler, when she was 5 years old.

Her path to modeling began while she studied art in Florence, Italy, where photographer Ugo Mulas discovered her in 1959. She adopted the name Veruschka and found an influential champion in Vogue editor-in-chief Diana Vreeland. She became a prominent face of 1960s and 1970s fashion, appearing on American Vogue covers and collaborating with photographers Richard Avedon and Irving Penn.

Her fame also brought film roles. She appeared as a version of herself opposite David Hemmings in Antonioni's 1966 movie "Blow-Up" and later played a poker player in the 2006 James Bond film "Casino Royale."

Art remained central to her work. She explored camouflage through body painting and developed staged portraits using costumes and invented personas. Berlin's Museum für Fotografie exhibited her "Veruschka Self-Portraits" in 2006.

Photographer Franco Rubartelli, her former partner and longtime creative collaborator, mourned her in a tribute, writing that she "wasn't just a great model. She was an elegant woman, sensitive, brave, with a beauty that did not stay in the camera, it would get into the soul of whoever watched her." He ended his tribute with a wish: "May the light of her memory never fade."

Sources: USA TODAY; The Hollywood Reporter; Vogue; Bild.
